[6 marks]

A drawer has 50 socks. 15 are black, 20 are white and the rest are grey. (a) Work out the probability that a sock picked at random is grey. Give your answer as a percentage. (b) Aisha takes out a white sock and keeps it. She then picks a second sock at random. Ben says, "The chance of a white sock is now smaller than it was." Is Ben right? You must show your working.

Hint

Answer

After: 49 socks, 19 white.

Answer: (a) 30% (b) Yes: 0.388 < 0.4

[6 marks]

At a fair, you pay £2 to play a game. Bag A and bag B each have five balls numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. You take one ball at random from each bag and add the numbers. If the total is 9 or more you win £10. 100 people play. (a) Find P(winning). (b) How many wins are expected? (c) Does the stall make a profit or a loss? How much?

Hint

Answer

25 outcomes. Count 9 and 10.

Answer: 0.12; 12 wins; £80 profit
